$comment: Feed registry. Every URL was verified reachable AND parseable on 2026-07-29; re-check anytime with `npm run check-sources`. Add a source by appending an object — no code change needed. `category` must match an id in `categories`.

$excluded.lobste.rs: Deliberately excluded. robots.txt is `User-agent: * / Disallow: /` (named search engines only) and the site emits `Content-Signal: ai-input=no, ai-train=no`. The feed returns 200, but fetching it with a custom bot goes against the operator's stated wishes.
$excluded.reddit.com/r/*/.rss: Excluded: 403 without a browser UA and intermittent 429 even with one (2 of 5 fetches succeeded at 4s spacing). Reddit directs automated consumers to registered OAuth API access. Not worth a credential for a news panel.
$excluded.eventmanagerblog.com/feed: Excluded: the domain was repurposed. It still serves valid RSS, but the feed title is now 'Crypto Casinos'. A status-code check alone would have accepted it.
$excluded.azurecomcdn.azureedge.net/en-us/updates/: Excluded: returns HTTP 200 with an `image/vnd.microsoft.icon` body — a favicon, not a feed. Use the releasecommunications API URL below instead.
$excluded.shopify.engineering, uber.com/blog/engin: No working feed found. Shopify serves an SPA HTML shell at .atom; Uber returns 406 to every UA tried; Anthropic has no feed at that path.

hackerNews.$comment: Algolia's HN Search API is public and key-free, and returns points/comments in one request — unlike the official Firebase API, which needs 1+N calls for 500 story ids. news.ycombinator.com/robots.txt sets Crawl-delay: 30 and does not disallow feeds; one request per run is well within that.
hackerNews.$trap: Use tags=front_page, NOT tags=story. With no `query` param the /search endpoint ranks by all-time popularity, so tags=story returns 2016-2024 classics ('Stephen Hawking has died', the xz backdoor) with HTTP 200 and healthy-looking item counts. They then vanish at the retention filter, so the collector reports 25 items and the dashboard shows zero.

devTo.$comment: Public, no key. The list endpoint returns description only; full bodies would need a per-article call, which we do not need.

github.$comment: Unauthenticated GitHub Search API allows 10 req/min PER IP — and on a shared/NAT address the separate `core` bucket (60/hr) is often already exhausted by others, so we only use `search`, which embeds the license object for free. In CI, always pass the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (30 search req/min). The REST search API does NOT support boolean OR between qualifiers — it returns HTTP 422 — so use one topic per query.
